chunks: And a group informed me from Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Safwani, who said: Shaykh al-Husayn ibn Rawh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me that Yahya ibn Khalid poisoned Masuh ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) with twenty-one dates, and he died from it; and that the Prophet and the Imams (peace be upon them) did not die except by the sword or poison; and it has been mentioned regarding al-Rida (peace be upon him) that he was poisoned, and likewise his son and the son of his son.
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Musa al-Kadim (a.s.) die and what is the pattern of martyrdom for the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the specific mode of Imam Musa al-Kadim’s martyrdom via poisoned dates, administered by Yahya ibn Khalid al-Baridi, reinforcing the Shia doctrine of *al-Shahada* (martyrdom) over natural death for the Ahl al-Bayt. It extends this pattern to Imam al-Rida and his progeny, underscoring the political persecution they faced from the Abbasid caliphs, thereby validating their status as divinely appointed leaders who were eliminated to prevent their influence from growing.
